text:
Priya (SE): opening thread for ApexLogistics POC — they need streaming chat with server-side tool calls into their shipment API, strict JSON-LD output, and Java + Python SDK examples. Key asks: ephemeral creds rotation, idempotent tool-call retries, schema validation with human-readable errors, pricing comparison (hosted per-token vs reserved pool + burst credits), and SOC2/KMS/QS details.
Anya (AE): they expect ~200 rps peak for routing queries during business hours, avg reply 130 tokens. Primary concern: deterministic JSON-LD for downstream ETL. Procurement asks if we support customer-managed keys (EKM) and an addendum.
Jorge (Eng): for 200 rps @130 tokens we usually advise a 1-node Dedicated pool with autoscale buffer for headroom; hosted pilot OK but tail latency could spike. If p95 <250ms is required, Dedicated + prefix KV caching recommended.
Priya (SE): target SLA p95 <250ms. They also want tooling to detect schema drift and fail-fast. Can Redwood return a validation error and emit violation events?
Jorge (Eng): yes — enable structured_output_mode with schema=JSON-SCHEMA-draft7 (or JSON-LD context) and action=reject. Service returns 422 + validation details (human_message + path errors) and emits schema_violation webhook. We can also auto-route raw output to a review topic.
Luca (Security): webhook hardening: prefer publishing tool-call payloads to a customer-owned queue (SQS/Kafka). If direct webhooks: require mTLS, IP allowlist, rotating webhook signing tokens (recommend 12h rotation), minimum TLS1.2+. EKM: Private supports customer KMS/HSM; Dedicated can negotiate EKM addendum. Hosted uses Redwood KMS by default. SOC2: we are SOC2 Type II — will paste standard boilerplate.
Priya (SE): they asked about tool-call idempotency and retries if their internal API is slow. Any guidance?
Jorge (Eng): pattern: SDK surfaces toolCall with idempotency_key. Customer should ack receipt and respond 202 + callback later. SDK has helper to correlate tool-call responses and handle retries; server side we support exponential backoff + max-retries policy. For streaming backpressure, use chunked delivery and advisory low-water marks; SDK exposes flow-control API.
JavaSDKBot: Java example (streaming + token provider + toolcall handling):
```java
RedwoodClient client = RedwoodClient.builder().tokenProvider(tokenProvider).build();
try (Stream<StreamEvent> s = client.chatStream("apex-ship-1", opts)) {
  s.forEach(ev -> { if (ev.isToolCall()) handleTool(ev.getToolPayload()); else System.out.print(ev.getDeltaText()); });
}
```
Priya (SE): nice. Also they want ephemeral token rotation: recommended TTL and broker pattern?
Jorge (Eng): STS broker pattern: Redwood issues short-lived tokens (TTL=15m default). Customer runs credential-broker (container/lambda) that exchanges service principal for STS token; TokenProvider refreshes when TTL <60s. We'll share sample broker (AWS/GCP/Azure).
Anya (AE): pricing: can we present hosted per-token estimate + reserved 1-node monthly quote with burst credits to handle peak? They want a simple comparison for procurement by EOD.
Jorge (Eng): rough calc: tokens = rps * avg_tokens * seconds_per_day * days. For 200 rps, 130 tokens, 8h/day pilot -> ~6.7B tokens/month (30d). Hosted = $X per 1M tokens; reserved = node monthly + lower unit + optional burst credits. Ill prepare two scenarios (8h/day pilot and 24/7 pilot) and include a note on streaming vs non-streaming (no separate stream surcharge).
Luca (Security): blockers: need EKM wording for contract, SOC2 evidence, webhook mTLS checklist, and confirmation on ephemeral rotation patterns.
Priya (SE): next steps: 1) Anya confirm pilot hours & legal contact; 2) Jorge produce back-of-envelope reserved quote + runbook + broker sample; 3) Luca draft SOC2/KMS + webhook hardening text; 4) schedule 30m tech kickoff (Tue).
Anya (AE): will confirm pilot hours & legal POC by 3pm PT.
Jorge (Eng): will drop quote + 1-node tuning checklist + sample broker (link) by tomorrow AM.
Luca (Security): will post SOC2/KMS wording and webhook mTLS/IP allowlist guidance in the questionnaire doc.
Priya (SE): thanks team :thumbsup: tagging @Jorge @Luca @JavaSDKBot for deliverables.
